UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the Claritas AI application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

registrationDate.description: Date and time when the user registered.

FinancialAccount.title: FinancialAccount
FinancialAccount.description: Represents a financial account (e.g., bank account, credit card) linked to a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the financial account.

accountName.description: Name of the financial account (e.g., 'Checking Account', 'Visa Credit Card').

accountType.description: Type of the financial account (e.g., 'bank', 'credit card', 'investment').

balance.description: Current balance of the financial account.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a financial transaction associated with a financial account.

transactionDate.description: Date and time of the transaction.

FinancialGoal.title: FinancialGoal
FinancialGoal.description: Represents a financial goal set by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the financial goal.

goalName.description: Name of the financial goal (e.g., 'Save for a down payment', 'Pay off debt').

targetAmount.description: Target amount for the financial goal.

currentAmount.description: Current amount saved towards the financial goal.

targetDate.description: Target date for achieving the financial goal.

AiInsight.title: AiInsight
AiInsight.description: Represents an AI-generated financial insight for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AI insight.

insightType.description: Type of the AI insight (e.g., 'Spending Recommendation', 'Investment Suggestion').

relevanceScore.description: Relevance score of the AI insight (0-1).

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the AI insight was generated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and ease of debugging, following the core design principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization. For instance, access control data for FinancialAccounts, Transactions, FinancialGoals, and AiInsights are kept under the user's profile to avoid using `get()` calls in security rules.

Structural Segregation is applied by storing user-specific data like profiles, financial accounts, transactions, goals, and insights in separate collections under each user's document. This allows for homogeneous security postures within each collection, as all documents share similar access requirements.

Access Modeling is standardized using hierarchical paths for user-owned data, such as `/users/{userId}/financialAccounts/{accountId}`, `/users/{userId}/transactions/{transactionId}`, `/users/{userId}/financialGoals/{goalId}`, and `/users/{userId}/aiInsights/{insightId}`. This structure simplifies ownership-based security rules.

The structure supports the required QAPs by ensuring that list operations are secure. Since each subcollection is scoped to a specific user, listing documents within these subcollections is inherently limited to that user's data, preventing unauthorized access to other users' information.
